note: Adapted from the species-level description no. 163 in Chhotani (1997), The Fauna of India: Isoptera. Original in English; only the soldier is known, the alate is recorded as unknown, and workers and nymphs are lacking; synonymic lists, bibliographic citations, figure numbers and distribution records are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule subrectangular, sides nearly parallel; antennae 13-segmented, 2nd segment equal to the sum of the 3rd and 4th, 3rd segment shortest; labrum about as long as wide, posterior sides nearly straight, narrowing forward to a broad apex; mandibles short, strongly hooked, coarsely serrate, much shorter than the head capsule; postmentum rod-like; pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior and posterior margins with weak to distinct emarginations.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellowish brown; antennae paler than the head capsule; mandibles dark reddish brown; remainder of the body yellow. Head sparsely pilose, pronotum slightly more densely pilose. Body length about 4.3–5.3 mm. Head capsule subrectangular, sides nearly parallel (length with mandibles 2.29–2.58 mm, to mandible base 1.48–1.74 mm, maximum width 0.81–0.95 mm). Antennae 13-segmented; 2nd segment equal to the sum of the 3rd and 4th, 3rd segment shortest. Labrum about as long as wide, posterior sides nearly straight, narrowing forward to a broad apex. Mandibles short, strongly hooked, coarsely serrate; much shorter than the head capsule (length 0.89 mm). Postmentum rod-like (length 0.81–0.89 mm, maximum width 0.29–0.31 mm, waist width 0.21 mm). Pronotum saddle-shaped; anterior and posterior margins with weak to distinct emarginations (length 0.28–0.37 mm, width 0.55–0.63 mm).
